original_question: A group G is called an orientable Poincaré duality group of dimension n over a ring R if it is of type FP over R and Hi(G; RG) = 0 for i ̸= n, while Hn(G; RG) = R as an RG-module, where the action on R is trivial. (Note that G is not required to be finitely presented.) If G is an orientable Poincaré duality group of dimension n over all fields, is it an orientable Poincaré duality group over the integers?
target_in_paper: No exact match exists in arXiv:1401.0300: that identifier is the Kourovka Notebook, not a paper with Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 on Poincaré-duality groups. The draft instead most closely matches Theorem B in Section 5.2 of arXiv:2506.14666, Virtual fibring of Poincaré-duality groups, together with the dimension-4 sharpening Corollary C / Theorem 5.9.
correct_elements: The draft correctly uses the Bieri–Dicks–Dunwoody style definition of an orientable Poincaré-duality group over a commutative ring R: type FP over R, vanishing of H^i(G;RG) outside the top degree, top cohomology isomorphic to R, and trivial orientation action. It also correctly notes that finite presentability is not required in this definition, which the paper explicitly adopts. Finally, it correctly isolates the coefficient-change issue between 'over all fields' and 'over the integers,' which is a real distinction in the paper.

The paper requires G to be an RFRS orientable Poincaré-duality group of dimension n; your draft omits the RFRS hypothesis entirely.

The paper concerns the kernel ker φ, not G itself, and the kernel has dimension n−1, not n.
Theorem B is an equivalence, not a one-way implication: it is equivalent to vanishing of β_i^(2)(G;K) for all i and all prime fields K.
In the paper, 'over all fields' on the Poincaré-duality side is paired with checking the homological criterion only over prime fields, using base-change for Poincaré duality.
The paper does not state or prove the general implication 'orientable PD_n over all fields implies orientable PD_n over Z'.
What the paper does prove integrally is a special low-dimensional upgrade: in dimension 4, the kernel can be concluded to be an orientable PD_3-group over Z (Corollary C / Theorem 5.9).
The paper works in greater generality with Poincaré-duality pairs, and the group case is a specialization of that framework.
The coefficient ring is assumed commutative in the Poincaré-duality subsection; if no coefficient ring is specified, the paper's default convention is Z.
refined_question: Let G be an RFRS orientable Poincaré-duality group of dimension n (with coefficients in Z unless another commutative coefficient ring is specified). Is the following equivalent to vanishing of all field-valued L^2-Betti numbers over prime fields: there exist a finite-index subgroup G0 ≤ G and an epimorphism φ:G0→Z such that ker φ is an orientable Poincaré-duality group of dimension n−1 over all fields? Equivalently, are the following two conditions equivalent: (i) there exist G0 and φ as above with ker φ orientable PD_{n−1} over every field; and (ii) β_i^(2)(G;K)=0 for every i and every prime field K?
justification: I checked the supplied arXiv ID first and found that arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, so it does not contain the Poincaré-duality setup, labels, or results your draft points to. The mathematical content of the draft instead aligns with Virtual fibring of Poincaré-duality groups: Definition 2.6 gives the paper's coefficient-ring-sensitive PD_n notion and explicitly says finite presentability is not required; Proposition 2.9 and Remark 2.10 supply the nearby structural facts and the base-change principle from prime fields to all fields; Theorem B in the Introduction and again in Section 5.2 is the paper's official statement whose conclusion involves a kernel that is orientable PD_{n−1} over all fields; and Theorem 5.9 / Corollary C explains why an integral conclusion appears only in dimension 4. So the draft is not paper-faithful as written: it extracts an implicit coefficient issue but drops the central RFRS/virtual-fibring/L^2-homology content. The sharp stand-alone reformulation should therefore be Theorem B, not the broader unproved implication from 'all fields' to 'Z'.
